label: input r/g mid-way through the original sequence (positions 3-7)
explanation: Very sparse unit (about 0.03% of steps). Nearly all activation mass (99.6%) is in the original-input phase at positions 3-7, peaking at positions 4-5; it never fires at t<3 and never in the copy phase (5 weak hits on <DEL>). The input token is almost always r or g (about 90% of mass; i and the digit 3 contribute a little). So it is necessary-ish but far from sufficient: only about 1.5% of r/g inputs at t>=3 activate. Whether a given r/g crosses threshold depends on soft context factors that raise the rate: the previous input being k/j/r/g (5-7x lift), the first token of the sequence being 1 or z (6-9x lift), and position 4-5. Stacking these conditions raises precision to about 0.39 but cuts recall to about 0.19, so no single crisp predicate describes it; it looks like a threshold over a sum of token-identity and context contributions. Top activations (e.g. 1 q n r k [r], 1 z 2 j j [g]) all fit r/g at position 4-5 after k/j/r and with first token 1/z. Does not fire on copy-phase outputs, early positions, or other letters.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=1 (+4.22), orig0=z (+3.38), prev_tok=r (+2.92), prev_tok=k (+2.86), orig1=w (+2.67), prev_tok=g (+2.63). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-2.25), phase=2 (-1.33), orig_idx=-1 (-0.87).
